definition: Mojo is a programming language for Linux and macOS.
details: It is a systems programming language with semantics inspired by Rust such as static typing and a borrow checker, but uses a syntax designed to be reminiscent of Python (like Nim and Julia). It was originally intended to be a superset of Python, but this goal has been either abandoned or postponed indefinitely as of March 2026. In May 2026, Modular launched a website for the language and in August 2026 Modular released Mojo 1.0, declaring it open source. Mojo builds on the Multi-Level Intermediate Representation (MLIR) compiler software framework, instead of directly on the lower level LLVM compiler framework used by languages like Julia, Swift, C++, and Rust. MLIR is a newer compiler framework that allows Mojo to exploit higher level compiler passes unavailable in LLVM alone, and allows Mojo to compile down and target more than only central processing units (CPUs), including producing code that can run on graphics processing units (GPUs), Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) and other accelerators. explainer.lead: Mojo is a systems programming language for Linux and macOS mixing Rust-inspired semantics with Python-like syntax. It matters because it aims to bring static typing and borrow checking to code written in a Python-familiar style.

tiers.eli5: A language that looks and reads like Python but carries stricter built-in safety checks, like a car with a familiar dashboard and better brakes.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers get static typing and a borrow checker with syntax reminiscent of Python, in the vein of Nim and Julia. A pitfall is planning around Python superset compatibility: that goal has been abandoned or postponed indefinitely as of March 2026.
tiers.paperLevel: Mojo is a statically typed systems language with Rust-inspired semantics and a borrow checker, built on the Multi-Level Intermediate Representation; its stated Python-superset goal is abandoned or postponed as of March 2026.

explainer.example: Mojo 1.0 was released by Modular in August 2026 and declared open source, after a language website launched in May 2026.
